# Collection room material sources

Downloaded 2026-10-07. Materials are bundled locally; the room has no third-party network dependency at runtime.

Photographic texture maps are original Poly Haven assets, licensed CC0:
https://polyhaven.com/license

- Oak Veneer 01 — Jenelle van Heerden
  https://polyhaven.com/a/oak_veneer_01
  1K diffuse/sRGB, OpenGL normal/linear, roughness/linear. Used for furniture and floor. The original scan is tinted to match the warm oak in the user reference, with vertical grain on cabinet backs and longitudinal grain on joinery.
- White Plaster 02 — Rob Tuytel
  https://polyhaven.com/a/white_plaster_02
  1K OpenGL normal and roughness. The room uses an ivory paint color over the scanned plaster relief; the original gray diffuse color is not used.
- Fabric Pattern 05 — Rob Tuytel
  https://polyhaven.com/a/fabric_pattern_05
  1K OpenGL normal and roughness. Used for unbleached linen relief. Original plaid color is not used.
- Wool Boucle — photographed by colormass, processed by Rico Cilliers
  https://polyhaven.com/a/wool_boucle
  1K OpenGL normal and roughness. Used for cream looped cotton/wool relief together with actual raised tuft geometry. Original multicolor checker albedo is not used.

API manifests used to resolve the exact official files:
https://api.polyhaven.com/files/oak_veneer_01
https://api.polyhaven.com/files/white_plaster_02
https://api.polyhaven.com/files/fabric_pattern_05
https://api.polyhaven.com/files/wool_boucle

Ceramic speckles, cork granules, neutral yarn variation, and leaf veins are original deterministic procedural texture canvases in collection-materials.js. These are not claimed to be scanned images.

Glass and brass use Three.js physical surface materials and the app's existing studio environment.
